title: should
subtitle: You should / You shouldn't
summary: Use should to say what is a good thing to do, and shouldn't to say what is not a good thing to do.

lesson.heading: You shouldn't watch TV so much
lesson.text: A young man sits in front of the television all evening. His mother points at him and says: 'You **shouldn't watch** TV so much.' After **should** and **shouldn't** we use the verb with no *to*.

lesson.heading: The form
lesson.note: **should** is the same for every subject, and **shouldn't** = should not.

lesson.heading: You should do it
lesson.text: You **should** do something = it is a good thing to do, it is the right thing to do. We often use it to give advice.

examples.text: Tom doesn't study enough. He **should study** harder.
It's a good film. You **should go** and see it.
When you play tennis, you **should** always **watch** the ball.

lesson.heading: You shouldn't do it
lesson.text: You **shouldn't** do something = it is not a good thing to do. **Shouldn't** = should not.

examples.text: Tom **shouldn't go** to bed so late.
You watch TV all the time. You **shouldn't watch** TV so much.
He eats too much. He **shouldn't eat** so much.

lesson.heading: I think ... should ...
lesson.text: We often say **I think ... should ...** and **I don't think ... should ...** to give an opinion. For a question we say **Do you think ... should ... ?**

examples.text: **I think** Lisa **should buy** some new clothes.
examples.note: = I think it is a good idea.

examples.text: It's late. **I think** I **should go** home now.
**I don't think** you **should work** so hard.
examples.note: = I don't think it is a good idea.

examples.text: A woman is trying on a big hat in a shop. She asks her friend: '**Do you think** I **should buy** this hat?'
What time **do you think** we **should go** home?

left.label: should
left.text: It is a good thing to do.
examples: It's a **good** film. You **should** go and see it.

right.label: must (stronger)
examples: It's a **fantastic** film. You **must** go and see it.
I'm very hungry. I **must** eat something.

lesson.heading: ought to
lesson.text: Another way to say **should** is **ought to**. The meaning is the same.

examples.text: It's a good film. You **ought to go** and see it.
I think Lisa **ought to buy** some new clothes.

lesson.text: Never put *to* after should: *You should go*, not ~~You should to go~~. Only *ought* takes *to*.

exercises.prompt: It's late and you're very tired. You ___ to bed.
exercises.explanation: should + verb with no to: You should go to bed.

exercises.prompt: Fruit and vegetables are good for you. ___ plenty of fruit and vegetables.
exercises.explanation: We use you should + verb to say what is a good thing to do.

exercises.prompt: Good advice or bad advice? Put each one in the right group.

items.text: wear a seat belt when you drive
go to bed when you're very tired

exercises.prompt: It's too far to walk from here to the station. ___ a taxi.
exercises.explanation: should has no -s and no to: You should take a taxi.

exercises.prompt: A man is eating a very big dinner. His friend says: 'You eat too much.' He ___ so much.
exercises.explanation: It is not a good thing to do, so we use shouldn't eat.

exercises.prompt: A woman is still at her desk late at night. You tell her: 'You work too hard.' She ___ so hard.
exercises.explanation: shouldn't = should not: She shouldn't work so hard.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of each sentence.

exercises.statement: Tom shouldn't to go to bed so late.
exercises.explanation: Tom shouldn't go to bed so late. There is no to after shouldn't.

exercises.prompt: You can't drive. You want your friend's advice. Put the question in order.
exercises.answer: Do you think I should learn to drive?
exercises.explanation: For a question we say Do you think I should ... ?

exercises.prompt: You don't like your job. You ask your friend: 'Do you think ___ another job?'
exercises.explanation: Do you think + I should + verb: Do you think I should get another job?

exercises.prompt: You don't need your car. I think ___ sell it.
exercises.explanation: I think you should ... gives an opinion about a good idea.

exercises.prompt: Sally and Dan are too young. I don't think ___ get married.
exercises.explanation: For a negative opinion we say I don't think ... should ... .
